name: Ocelot
tagline: Standards-obsessed Canadian SQL DBMS for Windows, written largely in assembly and open-sourced in 2001.
description: Ocelot was a SQL database management system from Ocelot Computer Services Inc., the Canadian company of SQL-standards author Peter Gulutzan, built to follow the ISO SQL standard closely: domains, constraints, stored procedures, collations, subqueries and an ODBC 3.0 interface, plus a front end. It ran on Windows and was written largely in x86 assembly with some C and Delphi. In 2001 it was published on SourceForge under a choose-one dual license, GPL or MPL, so users could pick either; the last file upload was in February 2003 and the DBMS has been dormant since. The company now makes ocelotgui, a GUI client for MySQL and MariaDB, so treat Ocelot itself as a historical curiosity.
statusNote: Last SourceForge release in February 2003; the company has since moved on to the ocelotgui MySQL/MariaDB client.

license.name: Dual GPL v2 or MPL 1.0 (user's choice)

strengths: Unusually faithful implementation of ISO SQL features for its size
Free under either GPL or MPL
weaknesses: Assembly-language codebase is hard to port or maintain
